text:
maya: Hey team — after the batch-header-normalizer deploy (~11:00 UTC) we're seeing a sharp spike in 5xxs for hosted inference. Initial look: auth header appears truncated for some requests, backend returns 500s. Canary slice was supposed to be 25% but errors are concentrated in us-west-2.

oncall-bot: alert: high_5xx_rate detected for /v1/generate (hosted) — 11:05 UTC — scope: canary

jorge: Acknowledged. Which flag/PR rolled?

maya: featuregate = batch-normalizer-v2 flipped on. Release window 10:58-11:02. No other changes.

shruti: Customer ticket from AcmeCorp reports 5xx starting 11:03. Repro (from their support note):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer AKIA...TRUNC" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: 502 with gateway log id x-request-id=rc-83a2. They say token was valid when retried.

kevin-sre: I pulled router traces for x-request-id=rc-83a2 and see header_normalize trimming long headers: `Authorization: Bearer AKIA...` -> truncated. Downstream auth proxy returns 500 due to parse failure.

kevin-sre: Also odd — canary assignment looks misapplied. Router config shows seed-tag mapping for us-west-2 set to canary=true across all seed ranges. Possible selector bug in rollout orchestration.

jorge: Copy. If canary applied broadly in that region, even a 25% global canary could hit 100% of some customers. We should rollback the flag and remove the canary routing for the region.

amanda-cs: On call with AcmeCorp now, they need ETA. Can support provide mitigation steps (retry/backoff) we can share while rollback proceeds?

support-ops: Suggest telling customers to retry with a fresh token for now; also advise to pin to a previous route via header `X-Route-Variant: stable` if they have that capability. Collect few failing request-ids and timestamps.

deploy-bot: rollback: featuregate/batch-normalizer-v2 -> false (initiated) by jorge at 11:12:02 UTC

jorge: Rolling back using orchestration CLI:
```
redwoodctl feature rollback --name batch-normalizer-v2 --scope canary --confirm
kubectl annotate config batch-normalizer rollout=rollback-1728604321 --overwrite
```
I will also remove the misapplied seed tag for us-west-2: `routerctl set-seed-tag us-west-2 canary=false`

maya: Kept sampling logs while rollback started. Samples show header_trim=true before rollback. After patching router seed tag, I'm seeing header_preserve for new requests.

kevin-sre: Rollback completed across control plane at 11:18:25 UTC. Metrics: 5xx rate for /v1/generate in us-west-2 dropped from 18% -> 0.9% over next 3m. Leaving alerts muted for 10m while we verify. :white_check_mark: :eyes:

amanda-cs: Thanks — relayed to AcmeCorp, they saw immediate improvement. They will send a few request-ids for our logs.

shruti: For postmortem: we need an invariant — ensure seed routing cannot make a canary global for a region without approval. Also add an additional validation that header normalization doesn't drop chars for Authorization.

jorge: Agreed. Action items: 1) revert PR and add integration test for long auth tokens (owner: eng-runtime) 2) add rollout validation for seed-tag overlaps (owner: eng-infra) 3) postmortem doc (owner: oncall). I'll open PRs.

support-ops: Collected failing request-ids from AcmeCorp: [rc-83a2, rc-83f9, rc-8401] — saved to support ticket.

deploy-bot: rollback finished successfully at 11:18:25 UTC — duration ~6m.

maya: Closing thread once postmortem linked. Thanks everyone.

kevin-sre: Will monitor for next hour and then close alerts.

oncall-bot: incident resolved (temporary) — next steps: postmortem due in 48h.
